title: Intro to csutil
text: Lists base R flexible. flexibility makes awkward check awkward take apart. csutil small set helpers four awkward jobs: splitting vector groups; pulling data frames nested named list; checking list actually holds; running function unique values vector instead every element. package deliberately tiny. seven exported functions nothing else.

code: counter <- new.env() counter$calls <- 0 counted_toupper <- function(v) {   counter$calls <- counter$calls + 1   toupper(v) }  x <- c("oslo", "bergen", "oslo", "tromso", "oslo") csutil::apply_fn_via_hash_table(x, counted_toupper) #> [1] "OSLO"   "BERGEN" "OSLO"   "TROMSO" "OSLO"  length(x) #> [1] 5 length(unique(x)) #> [1] 3 counter$calls #> [1] 1 scalar_only <- function(v) {   if (length(v) != 1) stop("this function handles one value at a time")   toupper(v) }  tryCatch(   csutil::apply_fn_via_hash_table(x, scalar_only),   error = function(e) conditionMessage(e) ) #> [1] "this function handles one value at a time" csutil::easy_split(1:4, number_of_groups = 3) #> $`1` #> [1] 1 2 #>  #> $`2` #> [1] 3 4

title: Intro to csutil
text: apply_fn_via_hash_table() extracts unique values input. calls given function , whole vector unique values, build lookup table. maps results back original input. function MUST therefore vectorised, counter shows. many values repeat, avoids redundant computation can much faster applying function element element.
code: input <- rep(seq(as.Date("2000-01-01"), as.Date("2020-01-01"), 1), 1000) a1 <- Sys.time() z <- format(input, "%Y") a2 <- Sys.time() a2 - a1 #> Time difference of 2.250466 secs  b1 <- Sys.time() z <- csutil::apply_fn_via_hash_table(   input,   format,   "%Y" ) b2 <- Sys.time() b2 - b1 #> Time difference of 0.3729157 secs
